## Decisions and assumptions
1. **Each trip has its own road network** (node/arc ids are local to the trip) -> everything is computed per trip; ids are never mixed across trips.
2. **Projection:** each trip is projected to its local UTM zone (EPSG 326xx/327xx) so distances are in metres (degrees are not distances).
3. **Cleaning:** only non-finite/out-of-range rows would be dropped (0 found). Gaps and odd timestamps are *flagged* (`gap_flag`), not dropped, so a prediction can be returned for every observation.
4. **Candidates:** all arcs within 100 m of a point, nearest 20 kept. Coverage of the reference arc on usable points: train 99.64%, student_test 99.99% (candidate miss rate on usable points 0.36% / 0.01%).
5. **Labels:** `.route` has no timestamps, so GPS points are aligned to the route with a monotonic dynamic-programming alignment (stay / advance 1-3 arcs). The label of a candidate is 1 iff it equals the aligned route arc. The route is a *reference*, not perfect truth.
6. **Unreliable labels (`label_ok = 0`)**: aligned arc further than 50 m from the point. train: 11.17% of points, student_test: 0.15%. These are excluded from training and from metrics. Worst train trips: 00000054 (11% usable), 00000033 (41% usable), 00000002 (88% usable). In 00000054 and 00000033 the track keeps going (slow/stationary, up to 19k points) after the reference route has ended, so the route does not cover the whole track.
7. **No leakage:** features use only the track and the road network; the route is used only to create labels. Scaling/normalisation is NOT applied here (fit it on train inside the modelling pipeline).
